<h>Lectio 3</h>
<c>D</c>ucentórum et quinque mártyrum, qui sǽculo décimo séptimo ineúnte, in Iapónia sánguinem pro Christo fudérunt, ad Philippinárum provínciam órdinis Prædicatórum magna pars attinébat. Primus, Alfónsus Navarréte, missiónis moderátor, qui, iníqua lege audácter sprete, fidélium necessitátibus públice subvénerat, Vómuræ, anno millésimo sexcentésimo décimo séptimo, cápite plexus est. Eódem anno atque sequéntibus úndecim, álii eiúsdem provinciæ patres, partim Nagasáchi, partim Vómuræ, mátyrii corónam percipérunt. Hanc prædicatórum cohórtem, aliósque ex ordínibus sancti Francísci, sancti Augustíni et Societátis Iesu, in cælum comitabántur et clérici et convérsi, fratrésque ac soróres tértii órdinis societatísque Rosárii, necnon et plures álii Iaponénses utriúsque sexus, quos omnes Pius nonus, anno millésimo octingentésimo sexagésimo sexto, Beatórum albo accénsuit.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Lavérunt stolas suas, et cándidas eas fecérunt
* In sánguine Agni,
<r>℣.</r> Isti sunt qui venérunt ex magna tribulatióne, et lavérunt stolas suas.
<r>℟.</r> In sánguine Agni,
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> In sánguine Agni,

<r>Te Deum</r>
<c>T</c>e Deum laudámus: * te Dóminum confitémur.
Te ætérnum Patrem * omnis terra venerátur.
Tibi omnes Ángeli, * tibi Cæli, et univérsæ Potestátes:
Tibi Chérubim et Séraphim * incessábili voce proclámant:
<n>(Fit reverentia)</n> Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus * Dóminus Deus Sábaoth.
Pleni sunt cæli et terra * maiestátis glóriæ tuæ.
Te gloriósus * Apostolórum chorus,
Te Prophetárum * laudábilis númerus,
Te Mártyrum candidátus * laudat exércitus.
Te per orbem terrárum * sancta confitétur Ecclésia,
Patrem * imménsæ maiestátis;
Venerándum tuum verum * et únicum Fílium;
Sanctum quoque * Paráclitum Spíritum.
Tu Rex glóriæ, * Christe.
Tu Patris * sempitérnus es Fílius.
<n>(Fit reverentia)</n> Tu, ad liberándum susceptúrus hóminem: * non horruísti Vírginis úterum.
Tu, devícto mortis acúleo, * aperuísti credéntibus regna cælórum.
Tu ad déxteram Dei sedes, * in glória Patris.
Iudex créderis * esse ventúrus.
<n>(Sequens versus dicitur flexis genibus)</n> Te ergo quǽsumus, tuis fámulis súbveni, * quos pretióso sánguine redemísti.
Ætérna fac cum Sanctis tuis * in glória numerári.
Salvum fac pópulum tuum, Dómine, * et bénedic hereditáti tuæ.
Et rege eos, * et extólle illos usque in ætérnum.
Per síngulos dies * benedícimus te.
<n>(Fit reverentia, secundum consuetudinem)</n> Et laudámus nomen tuum in sǽculum, * et in sǽculum sǽculi.
Dignáre, Dómine, die isto * sine peccáto nos custodíre.
Miserére nostri, Dómine, * miserére nostri.
Fiat misericórdia tua, Dómine, super nos, * quemádmodum sperávimus in te.
In te, Dómine, sperávi: * non confúndar in ætérnum.

b.a910fe786d:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>T</c>értio Idus Septémbris Luna décima. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>R</h>omæ, via Salária véteri, in cœmetério Basíllæ, natális sanctórum Mártyrum Proti et Hyacínthi fratrum, eunuchórum beátæ Eugéniæ. Hi, sub Galliéno Imperatóre, deprehénsi quod essent Christiáni, sacrificáre cogúntur; sed non consentiéntes, primo duríssime verberáti sunt, ac tandem páriter decolláti.
<h>L</h>egióne, in Hispánia, sancti Vincéntii, Abbátis et Mártyris.
<h>L</h>aodicéæ, in Sýria, pássio sanctórum Diodóri, Diomédis et Dídymi.
<h>I</h>n Ægýpto sancti Paphnútii Epíscopi, qui unus fuit ex iis Confessóribus, qui, sub Galério Maximiáno Imperatóre, dextro óculo effósso et sinístro póplite excíso, ad metálla damnáti fuérunt; deínde, sub Constantíno Magno, advérsus Ariános, pro fide cathólica, strénue decertávit; et demum, multis corónis auctus, in pace quiévit.
<h>L</h>ugdúni, in Gállia, deposítio sancti Patiéntis Epíscopi.
<h>V</h>ercéllis sancti Æmiliáni Epíscopi.
<h>A</h>lexandríæ sanctæ Theodóræ, quæ, cum incáute deliquísset, inde, facti pǽnitens, mirábili abstinéntia et patiéntia in hábitu sancto perseverávit incógnita usque ad mortem.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.1809b5f907:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>S</c>eptember 11th 2027, the 10th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Rome, upon the old Salarian Way, at the cemetery of Basilla, the holy brethren Protus and Hyacinth, both martyrs. They were eunuchs who belonged to blessed Eugenia.
<h>U</h>nder the Emperor Gallienus they were arrested on the charge that they were Christians, and, forasmuch as they could not be made to offer sacrifice, they were first grievously beaten, and then beheaded.
<h>A</h>t Leon, in Spain, (in the middle of the sixth century,) the holy martyr Vincent, Abbot (of the monastery of St Claudius.)
<h>A</h>t Laodicea, in Syria, the holy martyrs Diodorus, Diomede, and Didymus.
<h>I</h>n Egypt, holy Paphnutius, Bishop (in the Thebaid.) He was one of those Confessors who under the Emperor Galerius Maximinus had his right eye put out and his left hough cut, and was condemned to penal servitude in the mines. Under the Emperor Constantine the Great he strove stalwartly for the Catholic faith against the Arians, and at length fell asleep in peace, crowned with many crowns.
<h>A</h>t Lyons, (toward the close of the fifth century,) deceased the holy (Confessor) Patient, Bishop (of that see.)
<h>A</h>t Vercelli, (in the sixth century,) the holy (Confessor) Emilian, Bishop (of that see.)
<h>A</h>t Alexandria, (in the fifth century,) holy Theodora, who, having carelessly transgressed and deeply repented, continued unknown in the holy habit in wondrous self-denial and longsuffering, until her death.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
